source: story-briefs/gwf-75/mechanics_60.json (expert review, 2026-11-03), enriched with this module's game descriptions

language.label: story meaning, vocabulary, sound play and early reading

music.label: beat, rhythm, pitch, dynamics and making music

science.label: prediction, evidence, materials and living things

tap_scene.primary: Tap one large, highlighted in-scene object or tap each item once when counting.
tap_scene.alternative: Use a labelled bottom choice row or Next object control; preserve one-to-one counting state.
tap_scene.presentation: Base art stays fixed; valid hotspots get a gentle outline on request; state overlay only in the configured interaction region.
tap_scene.feedback: Immediately show a small local change or a counted mark and narrate what changed.
tap_scene.repair: If tapped twice or outside a target, keep progress; briefly indicate the active item without error sounds.

choose.primary: Tap one of two or three large illustrated choices; older children may see additional options.
choose.alternative: VoiceOver focusable choice list; switch-control access; one-choice-at-a-time display.
choose.presentation: Place choices in a readable tray anchored away from text and faces; selected option receives a ring and description.
choose.feedback: Show the consequence of the choice in the scene and explain the relevant property or perspective.
choose.repair: For factually checkable items explain the clue and allow retry; for open questions accept plausible options without marking emotions wrong.

assign_sort.primary: Tap an item then tap its recipient or category; drag-and-drop is optional, never required.
assign_sort.alternative: Two-step selection with large recipient buttons; automatic snap to the correct slot after deliberate choice.
assign_sort.presentation: Selected item floats slightly; recipient states reveal used/unused slots and completed groups.
assign_sort.feedback: Snap the item into a meaningful destination and describe who/what received it.
assign_sort.repair: Undo or reassign items freely; an occupied recipient shows a gentle “already has one” cue.

sequence.primary: Tap a card then tap a position, or use accessible move-left / move-right controls.
sequence.alternative: Numbered slots and move earlier/later buttons with VoiceOver ordering labels.
sequence.presentation: Show no more than a developmentally appropriate number of cards, each clearly distinguishable.
sequence.feedback: Re-enact the ordered story, pattern or word after placement.
sequence.repair: Allow rearrangement at any time; offer first-step model after repeated uncertainty.

snap_build.primary: Tap a piece and tap a broad snap zone; optional drag or rotate for older children.
snap_build.alternative: Cycle piece orientation with a large rotate button and place automatically on selected target.
snap_build.presentation: Protect scenery; draw minimal outlines, shadows and clear piece-state overlays.
snap_build.feedback: Snap with a subtle visual cue; play the resulting useful object animation.
snap_build.repair: Keep attempts reversible; do not penalise slightly imprecise placement.

quantities.primary: Use plus/minus buttons, tap-to-combine containers, unit tiles or stepwise pouring control.
quantities.alternative: Explicit increment/decrement and transfer buttons instead of freehand dragging.
quantities.presentation: Keep quantities and units visible; animate concrete changes rather than abstract score numbers.
quantities.feedback: Update both actual objects and any numerical or measurement representation together.
quantities.repair: Allow undo and reset-to-initial without losing story position; provide side-by-side comparisons.

music_audio.primary: Tap large pads, note choices, start/stop controls or sound layers to explore music.
music_audio.alternative: Show visual beat/pitch/volume cues and allow non-audio participation; do not claim this measures hearing.
music_audio.presentation: Use restrained animation synchronised to local audio; show a clear mute state and replay action.
music_audio.feedback: Echo, play back or layer the child’s contribution without success sounds or timing penalties.
music_audio.repair: Repeat sample on demand, allow slower playback and generous tempo tolerance.

navigate.primary: Tap connected map nodes or step arrows to move a character safely.
navigate.alternative: Previous/next destination list with descriptive landmarks; no precision drag.
navigate.presentation: Show one small readable route at a time, blocked paths distinguishable in more than colour.
navigate.feedback: Animate one short character move along the selected path and describe the landmark.
navigate.repair: Allow route reversal and safe exploration; never require timed navigation.

trace_draw.primary: Draw a short broad stroke or choose pre-authored marks; drawing is expressive, not handwriting assessment.
trace_draw.alternative: Select a ready-made mark or trace with an enlarged guided path.
trace_draw.presentation: Place a separate drawing layer above protected illustration with clear erase/undo controls.
trace_draw.feedback: A character uses or responds to the mark in the story.
trace_draw.repair: Support erase and redo; no exact-stroke grading for early years.

authored_sim.primary: Tap or choose one test setting and play the resulting pre-authored scientific animation.
authored_sim.alternative: Accessible step-forward controls and narrated still frames for each state.
authored_sim.presentation: Only show scientifically checked, content-authored states; label fantasy when appropriate.
authored_sim.feedback: Contrast the initial prediction with the observed test result, without judging curiosity.
authored_sim.repair: Offer reset and replay; test one change at a time wherever the learning objective requires it.

math.count-to-3.label: count a small set to three, one touch per thing
math.count-to-3.progression: point and say -> touch each one once -> say how many

math.count-to-5.label: count to five, one-to-one, in story order
math.count-to-5.progression: touch each once -> stop at the last one -> say the total

math.count-to-10.label: count to ten and notice one more
math.count-to-10.progression: count on -> one more makes -> compare totals

math.one-to-one.label: one for each: match one thing to each character
math.one-to-one.progression: give one each -> notice who has none -> say if there are enough

math.compare-more-fewer.label: which set has more, fewer or the same
math.compare-more-fewer.progression: see the bigger pile -> say more/fewer -> explain how you know

math.pattern-ab.label: continue a two-colour or two-shape repeat
math.pattern-ab.progression: say the pattern aloud -> choose what comes next -> make your own

math.pattern-abc.label: continue a three-part repeat
math.pattern-abc.progression: find the unit that repeats -> choose next -> spot a mistake

math.shape-match.label: match a shape to the space it fits
math.shape-match.progression: name the shape -> fit it -> turn it to fit

math.size-order.label: order three things by size or height
math.size-order.progression: big and small -> biggest/smallest -> order three

math.number-recognise.label: recognise a numeral in the scene
math.number-recognise.progression: find the numeral -> match it to a set -> say one more

math.position-words.label: in, on, under, next to, behind
math.position-words.progression: point where -> say the word -> put it there

lang.refrain-join.label: complete the book's refrain with the missing word
lang.refrain-join.progression: listen -> join the last word -> say the whole line

lang.rhyme-match.label: choose the picture whose name rhymes
lang.rhyme-match.progression: hear the rhyme -> pick the rhyming picture -> offer another rhyme

lang.vocabulary-picture.label: connect a story word to the picture it names
lang.vocabulary-picture.progression: point to it -> name it -> use it in the refrain

lang.opposites.label: opposite pairs met in the story
lang.opposites.progression: show big/small -> say the pair -> find another pair

lang.sound-words.label: sound words that belong to the scene
lang.sound-words.progression: make the sound -> match it to its source -> invent one

lang.initial-sound.label: hear the first sound of a word and find it in the scene
lang.initial-sound.progression: hear /s/ -> find the snake -> think of another /s/ word

lang.word-complete.label: build a short story word from its letters
lang.word-complete.progression: say the sounds -> tap the letters in order -> read it back

lang.retell-order.label: put three story moments back in order
lang.retell-order.progression: what happened first -> order three -> tell it in your words

music.steady-beat.label: keep a steady beat with the story
music.steady-beat.progression: tap along -> keep going -> count the beats

music.echo-rhythm.label: copy a short rhythm the character plays
music.echo-rhythm.progression: copy two taps -> copy a pattern -> make one for a friend

music.loud-quiet.label: choose loud or quiet to suit the scene
music.loud-quiet.progression: hear the difference -> choose for the scene -> explain why

music.high-low.label: tell a high sound from a low sound
music.high-low.progression: hear high/low -> find who made it -> sing one back

music.fast-slow.label: choose a fast or slow tempo to suit the scene
music.fast-slow.progression: feel fast/slow -> choose for the scene -> change it mid-song

music.long-short.label: long and short sounds
music.long-short.progression: hear long/short -> copy the pattern -> name it

music.instrument-sound.label: match a sound to the instrument or object that made it
music.instrument-sound.progression: hear it -> find it -> play it

music.play-refrain.label: play the book's refrain on an app instrument
music.play-refrain.progression: tap the guided notes -> play it through -> play it softly or faster

M01.name: Count and tap
M01.feel: The character needs to know how many. The child touches each story object once; it lights, nods or hops as the count is said aloud, and the last one lands the total.

items.role: one countable story object each, all fully visible in the safe zone

M01.target: the total as a word, e.g. 'five'
variation: why the character needs the number
what the last tap unlocks in the scene
never: counting things the character does not need
a timer or a wrong-answer sound

M02.name: One for each
M02.feel: Every character or place needs exactly one thing. The child gives one to each; the one left without is the story's small problem until it is matched.

items.role: pairs: the receivers and the things given, both in the scene

M02.target: who or what still needs one
variation: whether there is one spare or one missing

M03.name: More, fewer or same
M03.feel: Two visible sets; the story needs the bigger (or smaller, or equal) one. The child chooses, and the choice is used on the next beat.

items.role: two sets side by side, each countable at a glance (up to five each for 2-4)

M03.target: 'more', 'fewer' or 'the same', as the story needs
variation: whether the story wants more or fewer
how close the two sets are
never: sets too large to see at a glance

M04.name: Pattern next
M04.feel: Something in the world repeats (red, blue, red, blue) and has a gap. The child picks what comes next, and the path, song or row is complete.

items.role: the candidate pieces offered for the gap

M04.target: the piece that continues the repeat
variation: what the completed pattern lets happen
never: a pattern the child cannot say aloud

M05.name: Shape fit
M05.feel: A space in the scene wants a shape (a round stone for a round gap, a triangle sail). The child puts the right one in and the thing works.

items.role: candidate shapes, one of which fits

variation: the object that needs mending or completing
never: abstract shape sorters with no story reason

M06.name: Size order
M06.feel: Three things must go in order of size or height for the story to work (smallest in front, tallest at the back). The child orders them.

items.role: three clearly different sizes of one kind of thing

M06.target: the order the story needs, e.g. 'small, medium, big'
variation: which direction (small to big, tall to short)
never: sizes too close to tell apart on a phone

M07.name: Number spot
M07.feel: A numeral is somewhere in the scene (a gate, a door, a bus) and the story needs it. The child finds it and the number comes to life.

items.role: the numeral, drawn as part of the world

variation: a matching set nearby to count
never: a numeral floating over the picture

M08.name: Quick-look quantities
M08.feel: Glance at a small set and choose the matching tiny group without counting one by one.

items.role: two or three small groups of up to four, each visible at a glance

variation: dots, fingers or pictures as the match
why the character needs a quick answer

M09.name: One more, one less
M09.feel: The story needs one more or one less. The child adds or takes away a single object and sees the new amount straight away.

items.role: the set being changed, units clearly separate

variation: whether the count is said before and after

M10.name: Make the total
M10.feel: Two small amounts are combined to reach the total the character needs; the result is visible as one group.

items.role: the containers or groups being combined

M10.target: the total named in the story
variation: how far the parts are from the target

M11.name: Share fairly
M11.feel: A set is shared fairly between characters, one at a time, until everyone has the same.

items.role: the receivers; the shared items appear in a pile

variation: a remainder the characters decide about together

M12.name: Measure and compare
M12.feel: Two or three things are measured with the same unit (paws, sticks, ribbons) and compared to see which fits the story's need.

items.role: the things measured and the unit used

M12.target: longest, shortest or the one that fits

M13.name: Fill and compare
M13.feel: Containers are filled step by step and compared: which holds more, which is full, which is half.

items.role: the containers, filled in visible steps

M13.target: which holds more or which is full
variation: container shapes that mislead the eye
the story reason for the right amount

L01.name: Join the refrain
L01.feel: The book's refrain is said with its last word missing; the child taps the picture that finishes it and the line is said whole.

items.role: pictures of candidate words, one of which completes the refrain

variation: how the refrain's meaning has shifted on this page
never: a refrain the child has not yet heard twice

L02.name: Rhyme pick
L02.feel: A story word is said; the child picks the scene picture whose name rhymes with it, and the characters say the pair together.

items.role: pictures in the scene, one of which rhymes with the cue word

variation: how the rhyme helps the character
a silly near-miss among the candidates
never: invented words to force a rhyme

L03.name: Sound hunt
L03.feel: The character hears a first sound (/b/) and needs the thing that starts with it. The child finds it in the scene.

items.role: the target object and up to two visible near-misses

L03.target: the object beginning with the sound
variation: the object and why the story needs it

L04.name: Story order
L04.feel: Three small pictures from earlier pages are mixed up; the child puts them back in order and the character retells what happened.

items.role: three moments already shown in this book

never: moments the child has not seen yet

L05.name: Word build
L05.feel: A short story word (two or three sounds) is built from its letters in order; the word then appears on the thing it names.

items.role: the letters, in the scene (on blocks, stones, sails)

variation: the word and the object it labels
which letters are already in place

L06.name: Word to picture
L06.feel: A word from the story is said aloud and the child points to the thing it names in the scene; the character uses it straight away.

items.role: candidate scene objects, one of which the word names

variation: an everyday word or a new rich word
what the character does with it
never: a spoken answer required to continue

L07.name: Listen to the clue
L07.feel: A character gives a spoken or captioned clue and the child picks the picture it describes.

items.role: pictured candidates, one of which fits every part of the clue

variation: one-part clue for 2-4, two-part for older
a near-miss that fits half the clue

L08.name: What happens next?
L08.feel: The child predicts what could happen next from the picture; the story honours the choice before continuing on its path.

items.role: plausible next moments, pictured

variation: how the actual next page relates to the guess

L09.name: Clap the word
L09.feel: Clap or tap the beats in a story word (lan-tern, but-ter-fly) and hear it said in parts.

items.role: the word, shown with its picture

L10.name: Blend the sounds
L10.feel: Hear sounds said separately (/c/ /a/ /t/) and choose the picture they blend into.

items.role: pictures, one of which the blended sounds name

never: letter names in place of sounds

L11.name: Choose what to say
L11.feel: Choose what a character could say in a social moment; each kind option leads to its own reply.

items.role: short pictured lines a character could say

L12.name: Finish the description
L12.feel: Complete a description of something in the scene by choosing a describing word; the picture shows the chosen detail.

items.role: describing words, each true of something visible

variation: colour, size, texture or feeling words
never: words that are not visible in the picture

U01.name: Echo the beat
U01.feel: A character plays a short pattern on a scene object (spoon, drum, hoot); the child taps it back and the world answers in time.

items.role: the one scene object that is played

variation: two beats for 2-4, a pattern for 4-6
what answers the echo (rain, a bird, a door)
never: a pattern longer than four beats for 2-4

U02.name: Play the refrain
U02.feel: The book's own music moment: the character needs the refrain played, and the app's instrument screen opens over the page. Skippable, no microphone.

items.role: none: the instrument interface owns the screen

U02.target: the refrain's note sequence or song id
variation: tempo and dynamics asked for by the scene
never: a scene interaction or choice on the same page

U03.name: Loud or quiet
U03.feel: The scene needs a dynamic (a sleeping baby, a far-off boat). The child chooses loud or quiet and the characters play it that way.

items.role: the loud and quiet options, shown in the scene

variation: who is asleep or far away
what happens if played the other way (funny, never punished)
never: a wrong answer that upsets a character

U04.name: High or low
U04.feel: Two sounds, one high and one low; the story needs to know who made which. The child finds the maker in the scene.

items.role: the two sound makers, both visible

U04.target: which maker the story needs (high or low)
variation: which the story needs and why
a captioned visual cue when sound is off
never: a sound-only cue with no visual twin

U05.name: Fast or slow
U05.feel: The scene needs a tempo (tiptoe past the cot, hurry before the rain). The child sets fast or slow and the scene moves to it.

items.role: the thing whose speed changes

U06.name: Find the instrument
U06.feel: A sound rings out (ting, boom, rattle) and the child finds the object in the scene that made it; the character then plays it.

items.role: candidate sound makers in the scene

U06.target: the object that made the sound
variation: what is played once it is found
never: a sound-only cue with no visual twin

U07.name: Stop and go music
U07.feel: Music plays and stops; the characters move when it plays and freeze when it stops, and the child controls when.

items.role: the music control in the scene

variation: who freezes in a funny pose

U08.name: Create the soundscape
U08.feel: Layer gentle sounds (rain, wind, birds) to build the soundscape the scene needs; any mix is welcome.

items.role: sound makers visible in the scene

variation: the mood the scene asks for
never: sound-only participation with no visual twin

U09.name: Make your own rhythm
U09.feel: Compose a short rhythm by placing beat cards in slots; the characters play it back.

items.role: beat cards and the slots they go in

variation: long and short cards for older bands

U10.name: Match the musical feeling
U10.feel: Listen to a short piece and choose the feeling or scene it fits; several answers can be fair.

items.role: pictured feelings or scenes

variation: calm, busy, sleepy or bright music
what the choice changes in the scene

U11.name: Build the band
U11.feel: Add instruments one at a time to build a band for the story's moment; the band plays what was chosen.

items.role: the instruments available, each visible

variation: the occasion the band plays for

S01.name: Predict and discover
S01.feel: Predict what will happen, then watch the reviewed result; the story compares guess and result without judging.

items.role: pictured predictions

S02.name: Sort by property
S02.feel: Sort objects into groups by one property (floats, soft, made of wood) because the story needs them sorted.

items.role: the objects and two labelled destinations

S02.target: each object in the group its property fits
variation: what the sorted groups are used for

S03.name: Sink or float?
S03.feel: Choose an object to try in water and watch a reviewed sink-or-float result.

items.role: the objects that can be tested

variation: what the result means for the plan
never: encouraging water play without an adult

S04.name: Shadow match
S04.feel: Match an object to the shadow it would cast from where the light is.

items.role: shadows, one made by the object

variation: shape and size of the shadow

S05.name: Dress for the weather
S05.feel: Choose what a character should wear or bring for the weather shown; the character is comfortable outside.

items.role: clothing or items, pictured

S06.name: Help the garden grow
S06.feel: Give a plant what it needs one step at a time (water, light, time) and see reviewed stages of growth.

items.role: the care actions and the plant's stages

S06.target: the need the plant has now

S07.name: Follow the clues
S07.feel: Look closely at clues in the scene (tracks, crumbs, feathers) to work out what happened; more than one clue can be useful.

items.role: visible clues

S08.name: Test a material
S08.feel: Test two materials for a job (strong, waterproof, bendy) and watch a reviewed result before the characters choose.

items.role: materials to test

S08.target: the material that suits the job
variation: a fair test with one change

S09.name: Find a suitable home
S09.feel: Help a creature find a home that meets its needs; the child matches animal to habitat.

items.role: creatures and habitats, all visible

never: handling wild animals as an off-screen idea

S10.name: What makes it move?
S10.feel: Tap a push, pull, wind or slope and watch what makes the object move.

items.role: the object and the cause the child can apply

E01.name: How might they feel?
E01.feel: Notice how a character might feel from their face and body; any reasonable feeling is welcome and the story responds.

items.role: pictured feelings

E02.name: What could help?
E02.feel: Choose what could help a character; each kind choice leads to its own response.

items.role: pictured ways to help

variation: what kind of help (space, company, a tool)

E03.name: Ask for help
E03.feel: Help a character ask for help in a way that works for them (words, a card, a gesture).

items.role: pictured ways to ask

E04.name: Different perspectives
E04.feel: See the same moment from two characters' views; the child chooses whose view to explore and the story shows it.

items.role: the two characters' views

E05.name: Take turns together
E05.feel: The child and a character take turns placing or doing something together until the job is done.

items.role: the shared task's pieces

E06.name: Find a calming choice
E06.feel: Choose a calming thing the character can do (a breath, a blanket, a quiet corner); each is respected.

items.role: pictured calming options

C01.name: Build a solution
C01.feel: Build a solution from a few pieces (a bridge, a raft, a nest); different builds can work.

items.role: the pieces available

never: one correct build for open designs

C02.name: Find the way
C02.feel: Choose the route on a small map to get a character where they need to go.

items.role: route nodes and landmarks

C02.target: the route that reaches the destination

C03.name: Turn and assemble
C03.feel: Turn a piece until it fits and snap it into place; the object works once assembled.

items.role: pieces with a clear orientation

never: precision dragging as the only route

C04.name: Spot what changed
C04.feel: Spot what changed between two moments in the scene; the change matters to the story.

items.role: the changed details

C05.name: Invent a pattern
C05.feel: Invent a pattern with pieces from the scene; the characters use it (bunting, a dance, a path).

items.role: the pieces to pattern

C06.name: Plan the steps
C06.feel: Put the steps of a plan in order so the characters can do it.

items.role: the plan steps, pictured

C07.name: Draw a helping mark
C07.feel: Draw a broad helping mark (a path, a ribbon of light) or choose a ready-made one; a character uses it.

items.role: none: a drawing layer above the protected picture

C08.name: Choose and discover
C08.feel: Choose what the characters try or discover; the choice is honoured with its own consequence before the story continues.

items.role: pictured choices

variation: how it changes the next page
